text:
lina: Quick follow-up re: pin/rollout metadata. We hit a collision in staging: two tenants had the alias `preview` and a rollout that used `preview` ended up targeting the wrong tenant. Need clear namespace rules so rollouts are deterministic.

oscar: Can you paste the short repro? Is `preview` stored as a global alias or tenant-scoped?

lina: It's an alias in `tenant_aliases` table for tenant A and also a global alias someone created earlier. Rollout manifest referenced `alias: preview` without tenant_scope, resolver picked global alias because it appeared first in the lookup path.

mohit: Root cause: ambiguous alias lookup order. We currently do: tenant_pin -> global_alias -> model_catalog. That heuristic is too fuzzy. For rollouts we need deterministic scoping.

kat: Options: 1) require fully-qualified aliases in rollout manifests (tenant:alias) 2) change lookup order to prefer alias owner matching rollout scope 3) add alias ownership metadata + tie-breaker rules.

oscar: I like 2 + 3. Resolve against rollout.tenant_scope first, then global. But we must also prevent alias drift mid-rollout. If alias owner changes during an active rollout we get non-deterministic behavior.

mohit: Proposal for schema additions: alias object gains `owner_id` (tenant id or null for global), `immutable_during_rollout: bool`, and `version` int. Resolver should evaluate: 1) if rollout has tenant_scope -> look for alias.owner==tenant_scope, 2) else fall back to global alias, 3) finally fallback to model_catalog. If multiple matches, pick highest `version`.

kat: Picking highest version is deterministic but could surprise humans. Alternative tie-breaker is `owner match` then `creation_ts desc`. I prefer `version` for small surface area since we'll increment on explicit edits.

lina: Also: make alias resolution deterministic for the lifetime of rollout_token. If alias changes, new version won't affect requests tied to an existing rollout_token. That prevents mid-rollout drift.

oscar: Agree. For immutability we can disallow alias edits while referenced by any active rollout_token. Edits must create a new alias.version so you can revert. Ops can force-edit but that'll create an audit event and require two-step approval.

mohit: Migration plan: add columns `owner_id` and `version`. Backfill `owner_id=null` for older rows meaning global. For rows with a `created_by_tenant` we can try infer and set owner_id; limit to last 180 days. For ambiguous older aliases default to global and warn customers via console.

kat: Telemetry: add `resolution_reason` and `resolved_alias_version` to pin_resolution events so we can trace why a particular alias was chosen. Also a one-time probe: count cases where alias.owner != rollout_scope and rollout used that alias.

ci-bot: pipeline #2107: alias-schema-v1.1 dry-run scheduled on staging 1:00 UTC. Dry-run will emit `alias_mismatch_report` to #eng-sre.

lina: Docs: update alias resolution section with explicit lookup order, show examples for fully-qualified alias, and warn against relying on global aliases in tenant rollouts.

oscar: Action items: 1) PR for alias schema + migration (mohit), 2) resolver change + tests (oscar), 3) client/manifest validation (lina), 4) ops dry-run plan + rollback (kat). I'll create tickets and link here.

mohit: I'll draft the PR and include the dry-run query: `SELECT alias, owner_id, count(*) FROM rollout_refs WHERE alias IS NOT NULL GROUP BY alias, owner_id` to find ambiguous aliases.

lina: Great. Also add a small client-side warning when a manifest uses an unqualified alias and rollout_scope is set. Non-fatal but visible in debug logs.

oscar: Good guardrail. Thanks all :thumbsup:
